title: Cleaning personal computers, keyboards and screens
audience: Cleaning operative cleaning desks and workstations in an office or home, where the customer has asked for computer equipment to be included in the scope.
learningOutcomes: State which IT equipment is in scope for a cleaning job and confirm the scope before work starts.
Explain why water and silicone-based polish must be kept away from computer equipment, and why power must be switched off before the surface is cleaned.
Clean a keyboard, screen and computer base with a damp, not wet, cloth and a cotton bud in the gaps between keys.
Replace every item moved during the job so the customer's workstation is left as it was found.

instruction.heading: Scope first
instruction.body: IT equipment is often excluded from a general cleaning contract unless the customer names it as part of the work. That covers computers, monitors, printers, photocopiers, fax machines, televisions and similar equipment. Before starting, confirm with the customer or the contract whether the computer equipment is in scope. If it is not in scope, do not clean it, and record the decision. If it is in scope, follow this lesson.

instruction.heading: Why electronics need careful handling
instruction.body: Computer equipment is sensitive to dust, water and silicone-based polish. Liquid and polish can short-circuit components, leave a film that damages screens and key surfaces, and cause a fault that the customer will blame on the cleaner. Your job is to prevent water and polish from reaching the equipment, to keep electricity and liquid apart at every step, and to clean the surface only with the method set out here.

instruction.heading: Equipment and personal protection
instruction.body: Check that every item of equipment you use is clean and washed before use. Confirm that each chemical carries a legible manufacturer's label. Gloves must be worn at all times when using chemicals, and gloves and eye protection are needed when handling the cleaning solution. Keep windows or doors open where possible so that fumes from cleaning products do not build up in the room.

instruction.heading: Powering down safely
instruction.body: Always ask the customer for permission before switching off or unplugging a computer or monitor. Ask the user to remove any CDs or DVDs from the work area. Switch off the computer and the screen at the mains, then unplug them from the socket. Water and electricity must never come into contact, so do not wet the equipment or its power points at any stage.

instruction.heading: Cleaning the keyboard, screen and base
instruction.body: Remove surface dirt and debris from the keyboard with a mini vacuum or a soft, dry paint brush. Dust the screen with a dry, non-linting cloth to remove surface dirt. Apply the cleaning solution to the cloth, not directly to the equipment, and wipe the keys with the damp cloth. Clean between the keys with a cotton bud that has been dampened with the solution. Wipe the computer base with a damp cloth only if the base has been unplugged and is easy to reach. Never let the cloth drip, and never spray solution onto the screen or keyboard.

instruction.heading: Finishing the workstation
instruction.body: Replace any CDs or DVDs that were moved. Put back everything that was moved off the desk, in the same place, so the customer is not concerned about their property. If you switched off and unplugged the computer, plug it back in and switch it on again as the customer expects. Buckets and cloths must be washed, and stored colour coded. Buckets are stored upside down to air-dry, with cloths hung over them.

instruction.heading: Recording the job
instruction.body: Record whether the computer equipment was in scope, whether the customer gave permission to switch it off, which items were cleaned, and what was replaced. Note any fault, damage or dispute on the job sheet before you leave.

procedure: Confirm the computer equipment is in the scope of the job. If not, record that and leave it.
Check that the cleaning materials are labelled, and that the cloths and buckets are clean and colour coded.
Put on gloves, and open a window or door where possible.
Ask the customer's permission to switch off the computer and monitor, and ask the user to remove CDs and DVDs.
Switch off the computer and monitor at the mains and unplug them, keeping water away from the equipment.
Remove surface dirt from the keyboard with a mini vacuum or a soft dry brush.
Dust the screen with a dry, non-linting cloth.
Apply the solution to the cloth, wipe the keys, and clean between the keys with a damp cotton bud.
Wipe the computer base with a damp cloth only if the base is unplugged and easy to reach.
Replace any CDs or DVDs moved, return all items to the desk, and plug the computer back in if it was unplugged.
Wash the cloths and buckets, store them colour coded, and record the job.

workedExamples.situation: A customer asks for a home office desk to be cleaned, including the computer. The customer's contract covers general room cleaning and does not mention IT equipment.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Does the worker clean the computer, and how is the decision recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: The worker checks the contract and the customer's request. Because the contract does not mention IT equipment, the worker confirms with the customer whether they want it included, and records the answer. If the customer wants it included, the worker follows the procedure. If not, the worker cleans around the equipment and records that it was excluded.

workedExamples.situation: While cleaning the keyboard, a worker's cloth becomes wet, and a few drops of solution run into a gap at the back of the keyboard.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What does the worker do next?
workedExamples.reasoning: The worker stops, keeps the equipment away from further liquid, and does not try to power it on. The worker dries the outside gently with a dry cloth, reports the spill to the customer and the supervisor, and records it. The equipment must be checked before the customer uses it again.

equipmentAndPpe: Mini vacuum or soft dry paint brush
Non-linting dry cloth for the screen
Damp cloths for the keyboard and base
Cotton buds for between the keys
Approved cleaning solution, labelled and diluted as directed
Gloves, worn at all times when using chemicals
Eye protection, as the product requires

commonErrors.error: Cleaning the computer when it is not in scope, or without recording the decision.
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the scope before starting and record the decision on the job sheet.

commonErrors.error: Spraying solution onto the keyboard or screen, or letting liquid drip into the gaps.
commonErrors.prevention: Apply the solution to the cloth only, and keep the cloth damp, not wet.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning the equipment while it is still switched on or plugged in.
commonErrors.prevention: Get permission, switch off at the mains and unplug before cleaning, where the job requires it.

commonErrors.error: Leaving items moved off the desk, or discs out of their case.
commonErrors.prevention: Note each item moved and return all of them to their place before leaving the workstation.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Water and electricity must never come into contact. Do not clean powered equipment with a wet cloth, and do not wet the power points.
The source does not require a specific training record for this task. The employer may still require training before workers clean IT equipment; check the site rule.
Chemicals must be used as their label directs, with the safety data sheet available on site.
Stop and report if the equipment is damaged, if liquid has entered it, or if the customer does not want it switched off.

qualityStandard: Scope was confirmed and recorded before any IT equipment was touched.
Keyboard, screen and computer base are clean, with no liquid or polish residue on any surface.
No liquid entered the equipment, and no power point was wetted.
Every item moved during the job was returned to its place, and discs are back in their cases.
The equipment is powered as the customer expects, and the customer has confirmed the workstation is in order.
documentationEvidence: Scope confirmation for IT equipment, signed or noted by the customer
Record of permission to switch off and unplug each item
Chemical product and label reference used
List of items moved and returned to the desk
Any fault, spill, damage or dispute reported on the job sheet
summary: Confirm that IT equipment is in scope before you touch it, and record the decision.
Get permission, switch off at the mains and keep water and polish away from the equipment.
Apply solution to the cloth, not the equipment, and clean the keyboard, screen and base with a damp cloth.
Return every item you moved and record the job, including any spill or fault.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before switching off and unplugging a customer's computer, what must the worker do?
options: Wait for the customer to leave
Have a colleague sign the card

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must water and silicone-based spray polish be kept away from computer equipment?
options: They change the colour of the plastic case over time and make it sticky
The equipment is sensitive to dust, water and silicone-based polish
They make the screen display respond more slowly for the user
The plastic absorbs the scent and smells for a day or two

knowledgeChecks.question: How should the cleaning solution be applied to the keyboard?
options: Sprayed directly onto the keys so that it runs between them
Applied to the cloth, which is then used to wipe the keys
Poured into the gaps between the keys from the bottle at the desk
Dabbed onto the keys with a dry cloth and then wiped dry
